title: 🍃 My Use
body:
No matter how much you use, a break allows you to take a step back as noted above. 
Use this time to examine what you are getting when you use each week:
What is happening on that day that makes you want to use? 
What is the trigger for that day(s)? 

It is also helpful to examine what happens on the days you don't use. 
Do you have responsibilities that using could impact? 

🧖‍♂️🔎Whatever the reason, use this time for growth and intention. It is also important to remember that some of the messages may not exactly apply. Take what you can get and leave the rest.

title: 🍃 My Use
body:
Using a few days a week and not on other days, gives you a leg up on exploring why you use, what you get out of it, and what you may not. 

- What is happening on those days that make you want to use? 
- What is the trigger for those days? How do you feel the next day? 
- What is happening on the days you don't use?
- Do you have external responsibilities that using would impact? 
- What are those days like?  

It is also important to remember that some of the messages may not exactly apply. Take what you can get and leave the rest.

title: 🏡 My Triggers: Availability
body:
Times have changed, and now weed is everywhere.

🍃🌐In the past, getting it took effort, which naturally led to breaks. 
Increased availability makes quitting for any period of time tougher. This shift makes weed more like alcohol - it's present wherever you go. 
So, the responsibility is now on you, which can feel challenging.

Start by recognizing places you can steer clear of, as these are within your control. Then, focus on building your ability to resist by learning coping strategies, practicing strengthening meditations, and leaning on your social circle for support. 🤝

title: 😴 My Triggers: Boredom
body:
Boredom is one of the main reasons people have trouble completing a 30-day break.✅ 

Overcoming boredom requires :
1- planning activities (can be anything)
2- being spontaneous and getting out of your head by doing something in the moment, and
3- learning to embrace and appreciate boredom as a chance to clear your mind. 😤

title: 🎭 My Triggers: Shift Thinking
body:
Being creative is about the outcome, what you produce.Weed may actually make you more creative. 

It may make you think you are more creative when you are not. Whatever it is doing, focus on the outcome.

Is the weed a kickstarter or the reason you are creative? 

What happens if you put the same effort into taking a creative risk when not using it? What is the product then?

You value creativity, so be curious about what the next 30 days will create. 💡

title: 🍃 My Use
body:
Having a couple of days a week where you do not use gives you a leg up on exploring why you use, what you get out of it, and what you may not. 

- What is happening on those days that make you want to use? 
- What is the trigger for those days? What is happening on the days you don't use? 
- Do you have external responsibilities that using could impact or do you just need a break? 
- What are those days like? 
- Do you have hangover effects, and feel worse or better?

Now that you are taking a break, you can explore your relationship for real because, after 1-2 weeks or so, you can see what days are like without the carryover effects of the days you use.

title: 🍃 My Use
body:
Taking a break is most important for people who are using nearly every day. When we use every day, it is really hard to see what life is like without weed.It will likely be hard, especially in the beginning, because your brain and body haven't had any real time off to reset your endocannabinoid system. 

🧠🙅‍♀️ This is why you are here. Now that you are taking a break, you can explore your relationship for real because, after 1-2 weeks or so, you can see what days are like without the carryover effects of the days you use. For today, focus on your preparation for Clear30.

title: ✨ My Triggers: Enhancing Activities
body:
🍃Weed often makes everyday tasks less boring and can (or cannot) enhance certain things like music. 

To pretend that is not happening for some people is silly. 
But go in eyes wide open. Any drug will make everyday tasks less boring. 

The question is do you want to be reliant on a substance to do the dishes or watch a movie 🍽️🎥.

Is it making it better, is it making it more tolerable, or something in between? Clear30 allows you to explore what everyday life is like without weed.

title: 🙇‍♀️ My Triggers: I Like It
body:
It's okay not to exactly know what triggers you, other than that you just like being high right now. This is actually the exact reason for Clear30. 

It's like asking someone why they like their friends, and them saying, 'I just like them.' What about them do you like? 📝 What is that feeling when you are with them that makes you want to be with them?

title: 👥 My Triggers: Friends
body:
Many people mention that using weed has become a big part of their social life. For some, it becomes a shared experience and even acts like a bond between friends. 

Deciding to take a break might affect these friendships, especially if everyone isn't on the same page in their journey. 
However, usually, our real friends want us to succeed and be happy. 

To make the most of your Clear30, we suggest: 
1- Finding a friend who also wants to take a break. Doing it together can make the journey easier. 🤝💪
2- Letting your friends know about your decision - whether you are doing it alone or with someone. 

It's a good way to see who truly supports your choices, no matter what their own path might be.❤️🤗

title: 💖 My Triggers: Close Connections
body:
Our closest relationships provide us with a feeling of safety and the assurance that someone genuinely cares for us, and we for them.
This is why it becomes especially challenging when a close friend or partner encourages behavior that might not be in our best interest, like using weed.

🍃The most important step you can take is to have an honest conversation with them about your Clear30 intentions. Explain why taking a break from weed is essential for your well-being. 

🌟It might be beneficial for both of you to take a break together. This way, you can reevaluate the role weed plays in your relationship. If they decide to join you on this break, that's wonderful. 

However, if they choose a different path, that's okay too. Everyone has their unique journey.Regardless, it's crucial to discuss your feelings and seek their understanding and support. That's what loved ones do for each other. ✨🤝✨

title: 😓 My Triggers: Stress
body:
Stress is a trigger to use for many people. When we're stressed, substances like weed seem to offer quick relief and a sense of reward in our brains. 

🍃💨 However, there's a catch, often called the boomerang effect. 
While weed might have been effective at first, over time, it might only mask the problem without addressing the root cause of your stress. During your Clear30, proactively find alternative ways to manage stress before it takes hold. 

This might include exercise, meditation, focused breathing, and seeking therapy or coaching. The catch - it takes work! It is not a quick fix. Clear30 is designed to help make it easier for you to do things that are hard!

body:

Using weed regularly at your age not only increases your chance of mental health problems now but also increases your chance of problems later because your brain actually develops differently - and not in the good kind of way 🙇‍♀️😔. 

Be really proud of yourself and make sure your brain buys you a thank you gift.💚

title: 🧠 Age Matters
body:
Around age 28, we often re-evaluate our lives. We look at how our circumstances and the choices we make may be affecting our future. This makes it the perfect time to Clear30. 

It also matters now because the younger you are, the more weed affects your brain development. So, if you started smoking or using before you were 25, the consequences of use on your brain are worse. The great thing is they can be reversed in most cases. 🔄💪

title: 💆 Age Matters
body:
As we get older, we start to think about how our actions are affecting our own life and the lives of the people around us. 

⚖️ Reevaluating your use at mid-life allows you to evaluate more than just your cannabis use but also all aspects of your life and how cannabis relates to it.One of the things that will be important now is to ask yourself if weed is holding you back in any aspect of your life, whether it is your career, relationships, purpose, or just the clarity of thought.👨‍👧‍👦💚🧩

title: 💆 Age Matters
body:
Individuals in their 50-60s are one of the fastest-growing populations of cannabis users. 

Cannabis affects older adults differently than those in their 20s in good and bad ways. Generally (not always), the effects are more intense and potentially problematic by isolating you in your own world.

At your age, it is usually less social and more about an internal experience when you use more than occasionally. Whether it is for sleep, pain, or just to relax, now is a time to explore how you can get those benefits without cannabis while you are breaking.

You also should let your healthcare professional know how much you use as it may interfere with medications without you realizing it.

title: 🧟‍♂️ My Triggers: Pain Relief
body:
Studies have shown that cannabis can relieve pain. The question is not whether it relieves pain, but how it relieves pain. There is significant evidence that a portion of the pain relief is due to both placebo and shifting your mind away from the pain. 

🤍💡 During Clear30, examine other ways, especially mindfulness as well as OTC medications like ibuprofen or other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) if your doctor allows, to relieve pain. 
The goal of a break is to explore your pain and different ways to relieve it without cannabis over the next 30 days. 

After your break, it could be that you go back because it is the only thing that helps. After your break, you may realize it is a combination of factors that work. That is for you to decide. Good luck on your journey and be sure to speak with your doctor about your plans.
